## 2. Traps

### 2.1 Every GA4 fact here is unread

- No Google page has been read (Context7 skipped, M-021). Phase 0 reads
  Google's own pages in a browser, at no cost. Each row is recorded as
  confirmed or wrong, with its source URL, in `plan/analytics/phase0.md`:
  - **A.** the gtag `config` fields of Rule 2, including `cookie_domain`
    and `cookie_update`;
  - **B.** `ga-disable-<ID>`;
  - **C.** `cookie_prefix` and `cookie_expires`;
  - **D.** the enhanced-measurement, user-provided-data and granular-data
    toggles;
  - **E.** the data-retention options, and whether they govern explorations
    only;
  - **F.** the property access model and its roles;
  - **G.** the CSP hosts Google lists for GA4;
  - **H.** (S-A3) whether a history-change page view uses the
    `page_location` set by `config` or `set`, or `document.location`;
  - **I.** the measurement ID's shape;
  - **J.** `navigator.globalPrivacyControl` and `navigator.doNotTrack`;
  - **K.** where Google's GA data processing terms are accepted.
- A wrong fact stops the phase that needs it, and goes to the owner of the
  FR it breaks. It is not patched around.

### 2.2 Consent Mode is a trap for this design

- The standard snippet sets `gtag('consent', 'default', {…denied})` and
  loads the tag at once.
- With "advanced" behaviour, that sends cookieless pings before any choice,
  which fails FR-006 (Lex Q3.1).
- "Basic" behaviour still loads Google's script before the choice.
- This plan uses neither. The tag is simply absent until Allow.

### 2.3 A `<Link>` keeps the tag

- Next's client-side navigation keeps `window`, `dataLayer` and the loaded
  `gtag.js`.
- **Into a staff page**, a resident gtag.js could read guest PII on S-3,
  S-15 and S-16. `ga-disable` stops hits, not the script (S-A2). The guards:
  1. staff links as `<a>`;
  2. StaffFrame's reload (Rule 4), which holds whatever link a future edit
     adds.
- **Into an unmeasured guest page** (privacy, terms), no hit goes out
  because of `ga-disable-<ID>` on unmount and enhanced measurement OFF.
- **The walk** navigates S-1 → privacy (`<Link>`) → Staff login. It
  asserts zero hits after leaving S-1, and an admin document with no
  `googletagmanager` script.

### 2.4 The CSP of the first document is the CSP of the whole session

- A CSP header applies to the document that loaded it, and a client-side
  navigation keeps the first page's policy.
- So S-1's Google allowance reaches a privacy page opened with a `<Link>`.
  That is acceptable, because nothing loads there (Rule 4).
- It can never reach a staff screen. The staff screens always start their
  own document, because of the `<a>` links and the StaffFrame reload.

### 2.5 Cookies are per host, tenants are per path

- Every tenant is on one host (`/t/villa`, `/t/alteza`), so GA's default
  `_ga` cookie would be ONE client id across tenants.
- `cookie_prefix: 'ga_<slug>'` **[unverified]** gives each tenant its own
  cookies.
- `cookie_domain: 'none'` **[unverified]** keeps them host-only. GA's
  default `auto` would set the cookie on the registrable parent, where a
  host-only delete misses it (S-A4).
- `cookie_expires: 15552000` (180 days) with `cookie_update: false`
  **[unverified]** makes the cookie end 180 days after it was set, not 180
  days after the last hit. That is FR-008's "no identifier outlives the
  choice": the choice is also 180 days from when it was made.
- The deletion runs on every non-load decision (Rule 6). It expires every
  cookie with the prefix, on the host and on the parent domain.

### 2.6 `tenant_public()` is replaced for the fourth time (trap 20, trap 25)

- The 46th file drops and re-creates `tenant_public()` with
  `analytics_id`.
- `schema-welcome-text.sql` (the 44th) does the same with one column fewer.
  Its step 2 is guarded on `tenant_public()` returning `analytics_id`,
  exactly as `schema-legal.sql` was guarded on `welcome_text`.
- `schema-voice.sql` (the 41st) puts back a nine-key constraint and a
  `tenant_feature_on()` that knows only voice. A re-run after this file must
  skip both, so both are guarded on `tenants.analytics_id` existing.
- `audit_row()`'s `tenants` allowlist gains `analytics_id`,
  `analytics_instructed_on` and `analytics_since`. That is an edit to the
  43rd file, so the 43rd and every file after it are re-run in order
  (trap 25).

### 2.7 The version is bumped on the FIRST switch-on, not on every flip

- **Round 1 bumped `policy_version` on every flip.** Rhea's A-R5 and
  FR-019 say: bump on the first switch-on, and when the analytics text
  changes, not on every re-enable. The plan follows the FR.
- **The first switch-on** is the one that finds `tenants.analytics_since`
  null. The 46th file's trigger stamps `analytics_since = now()` and bumps
  the version in the same statement. It does this for every door: the
  platform route, a CLI, a hand.
  - A numeric version becomes n + 1.
  - A non-numeric one (the check allows `v1.2`) refuses the switch with a
    sentence: "Set the next policy version on the Legal tab before switching
    analytics on."
- **Later re-enables do not bump.** A guest's choice made under the first
  analytics text stays valid across an off-and-on, because the text it was
  made under has not changed.
- **A text change** is bumped by hand, on the Legal tab, as every
  privacy-text change is today (D-129). The plan makes it impossible to
  forget silently: `legal.test.ts` pins the analytics paragraphs, and the
  pin's failure message says "bump policy_version for every tenant with
  analytics_since set".
- **The audit:** the `tenants` update writes its own audit row
  (`policy_version` is in the allowlist already).

### 2.8 The bar is decided after hydration, so it lands one frame late

- The server cannot read localStorage, so the server and the first client
  render show nothing, and an effect decides.
- On S-6 and S-13 the bar is inserted above `<main>` one frame after the
  first paint. Uma's M-012 point 1 asked if that is acceptable: **yes**.
  - It lands before any field could hold focus.
  - A reserved slot would be a permanent empty gap for every guest who has
    already chosen (Vera: "no empty slot when hidden").
- The `role="status"` line is server-rendered and empty, outside the bar
  (Vera § 3.1).

### 2.9 A walk that sends real hits sends real data

- The walk never lets a request reach Google. Playwright routes
  `**/*google-analytics.com/**` and `**/*analytics.google.com/**`, records
  each request's URL and body, then aborts it.
- `gtag.js` itself is fetched from `www.googletagmanager.com`, a free GET.
  If it will not load for a test ID, the walk needs the walk property's ID
  (q5).
- The recorded payloads are the "raw events" of AC-11 and AC-15. The walk
  greps them for the PII strings it typed, and for every key outside the
  two lists.

### 2.10 Development and the CSP

- `next dev` needs `'unsafe-eval'` for its refresh runtime. So
  `securityHeaders()` adds it in development only, and the unit test pins
  that production has none.
- A Vercel PREVIEW deployment's toolbar (`vercel.live`) is blocked by the
  production CSP. That is accepted, and recorded in R-55.
- `middleware.ts` runs on the edge runtime. It reads `SUPABASE_URL` from
  `process.env` directly, and imports nothing `server-only` and not
  `lib/env.ts` (S-A9).
- It sets RESPONSE headers: `const res = NextResponse.next();
  res.headers.set(…)`. Passing `headers` to `NextResponse.next()` would set
  request headers (S-A9).

### 2.11 A brand image on a foreign host meets `img-src` (S-A6)

- `logo_url`, `banner_url` and `assistant_avatar_url` accept any `https://`
  host (`schema-roles.sql:165-166`, `schema-assistant-avatar.sql:18`).
- The CSP's `img-src` allows `'self' data: blob:` and the Supabase origin.
  A tenant with a logo elsewhere would lose it, silently.
- Phase 0 runs a read-only query of the three columns' hosts for every
  tenant, through the Supabase server (read-only, plan q9) or `psql`,
  SELECT only.
  - **If every host is the Supabase origin**, which is the likely case
    (D-123 uploads there), the 46th file narrows the three checks to
    `^https://<project>.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/brand-images/`.
    Because the project host differs per environment, the check is written
    against the Storage path, not the host: `'^https://[^/[:space:]]+/storage/v1/object/public/brand-images/[^[:space:]]+$'`.
    The platform form shows the constraint's words.
  - **If a live row uses another host,** that host is listed in `img-src`
    deliberately, by name, and recorded in R-55. The check is not narrowed
    for that row's tenant.
- Either way, the CSP is the browser's enforcement.

## 3. The data model

`packages/db/sql/schema-analytics.sql` is the 46th file. It runs in one
transaction, is idempotent, and is re-run in order after the 45th (§ 2.6).
Every function has `set search_path = ''` and qualifies every name
(trap 19). Every refusal is `check_violation` (23514) in words, which
`fromPostgrest()` maps to a 400.

```sql
-- 1. The tenth key, and no row = OFF for analytics as for voice.
alter table public.tenant_features drop constraint if exists tenant_features_key;
alter table public.tenant_features add  constraint tenant_features_key check (feature in (
  'dashboard','conversations','unanswered','suggested_questions',
  'booking_page','manage_booking','calendar','notifications','voice','analytics'));
create or replace function public.tenant_feature_on(p_tenant_id bigint, p_feature text) returns boolean
language sql stable set search_path = '' as $$
  select coalesce((select f.enabled from public.tenant_features f
                   where f.tenant_id = p_tenant_id and f.feature = p_feature),
                  p_feature not in ('voice','analytics'))
$$;   -- grants as schema-voice.sql

-- 2. The measurement ID (FR-020). Public by nature (it is in every hit), but handed out only while on (step 5).
alter table public.tenants add column if not exists analytics_id text;
alter table public.tenants drop constraint if exists tenants_analytics_id_shape;
alter table public.tenants add  constraint tenants_analytics_id_shape
  check (analytics_id is null or analytics_id ~ '^G-[A-Z0-9]{6,12}$');   -- the length is Phase 0 row I's
create unique index if not exists tenants_analytics_id_unique
  on public.tenants (analytics_id) where analytics_id is not null;      -- the race guard
--    tenants BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF analytics_id: another row holds it →
--      'That measurement ID is already set for another tenant. Each tenant has its own Google Analytics property.'
--    (the trigger gives the sentence; the index holds under a race, where fromPostgrest()'s 23505 is a 409
--     with platform.ts's generic words — accepted, two super users saving the same ID at the same instant)

-- 3. The written instruction (FR-028) and the gates on the switch.
alter table public.tenants add column if not exists analytics_instructed_on date;
alter table public.tenants add column if not exists analytics_since         timestamptz;
--    tenants BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF analytics_instructed_on:
--      a date after today in the tenant's zone → 'The written instruction date cannot be in the future.'
--      (the zone: tenant_applications' bookings config timezone, else 'Asia/Manila' — assumption T-A1)
--    tenant_features BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE, feature = 'analytics' and new.enabled:
--      no analytics_instructed_on → 'Record the resort''s written instruction on the Legal tab first.'
--      no analytics_id            → 'Set the Google Analytics measurement ID before switching analytics on.'
--    tenants BEFORE UPDATE OF analytics_id, analytics_instructed_on, while tenant_feature_on(id,'analytics'):
--      analytics_id to null            → 'Switch analytics off before removing its measurement ID.'
--      analytics_instructed_on to null → 'Switch analytics off before clearing the written instruction date.'
--    No exemption for service_role (unlike the DPA gate): a tool or a walk sets the date and the ID first.

-- 4. The first switch-on bumps policy_version (§ 2.7, FR-019, A-R5).
--    tenant_features AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF enabled, feature = 'analytics', new.enabled,
--    and the tenant's analytics_since is null:
--      numeric policy_version → (n + 1)::text, analytics_since = now(), in one UPDATE;
--      otherwise raise check_violation: 'Set the next policy version on the Legal tab before switching analytics on.'
--    security invoker: the super token can update tenants already (tenants_super_all, schema-roles.sql:185).

-- 5. tenant_public(), with analytics_id, NULL unless the switch is on (Rule 3, wall 2).
--    drop + create (the return type changes), the same body as the 44th file plus:
--      case when public.tenant_feature_on(t.id, 'analytics') then t.analytics_id end as analytics_id
--    still security definer, search_path = '', no archived tenant; grants re-applied.
--    analytics_instructed_on and analytics_since are NOT in it: they are between the platform and the resort.

-- 6. (Only if Phase 0's S-A6 query finds every brand image on Storage, § 2.11.)
--    tenants_brand_images: logo_url, banner_url and the avatar narrowed to the brand-images public path.
```

### 4.2 `apps/web/lib/analytics.ts` (pure, browser-safe, tested)

```ts
export const ANALYTICS_CHOICE_DAYS = 180;           // Lex Q3.3, FR-008
export const ANALYTICS_RETENTION_MONTHS = 2;        // Lex Q3.4, FR-024; the property setting, § 6.2
export const GA_COOKIE_SECONDS = ANALYTICS_CHOICE_DAYS * 86_400;
export const ANALYTICS_ID_SHAPE = /^G-[A-Z0-9]{6,12}$/;   // the SQL check's twin (S-A8); a test pins both strings equal
export type MeasuredPage = 'chat' | 'book' | 'manage';
export type StepEvent = 'chat_started' | 'quote_shown' | 'request_sent' | 'stay_found';
export const PAGE_TITLE: Record<MeasuredPage, string> = { chat: 'Chat', book: 'Booking page', manage: 'Manage booking' };
export interface StoredChoice { choice: 'allow' | 'decline'; at: string; version: string; via: 'bar' | 'privacy' }
export function choiceKey(slug: string): string;                                   // 'analytics:<slug>'
export function readChoice(raw: string | null, version: string, now: Date): StoredChoice | null;  // expired / other version / malformed → null
export function privacySignal(nav: { globalPrivacyControl?: boolean; doNotTrack?: string | null }): boolean;
export function decide(stored: StoredChoice | null, signal: boolean, writable: boolean): 'load' | 'ask' | 'none';
export function measuredLocation(href: string, page: MeasuredPage): string;          // S-13: origin + path, nothing else
export function measuredReferrer(referrer: string, origin: string, previousPage: MeasuredPage | null): string;  // external → its origin; else our origin
export function cookiePrefix(slug: string): string;                                 // 'ga_' + slug, [a-z0-9_] only
export function cookieDomains(hostname: string): string[];                          // the host, then its parent (S-A4)
```

- `decide()` returns `'none'` for any signal, unless the stored choice is
  `via === 'privacy' && choice === 'allow'` and valid.
- `decide()` returns `'none'` for unwritable storage.
- Otherwise, `decide()` returns `'load'` for a valid allow, `'none'` for a
  valid decline, and `'ask'` for no valid choice.
- The caller clears the cookies on every result but `'load'` (Rule 6).

### 4.3 `apps/web/components/analytics.tsx` (Client)

- **`<AnalyticsRoot analytics={…|null}>`** is a context provider placed by
  each Client Screen. With `null`, or with an ID that fails

  `track()` is a no-op.

  all a screen sees.
- **`<ConsentBar />`** is Vera § 3.1's markup exactly, with the polite

  The module flag holds the ID it configured.
  - **A first call:**
    - it sets `window.dataLayer` and `window.gtag`;
    - then it runs `gtag('js', new Date())` and `gtag('config', id,

    - then it appends the async script.

> Written 2026-10-28 by Theo (gate 5), against the working tree on

>
> Read [§ 0](#0-the-eight-rules) first.

---

## What this plan covers

| | |
|---|---|
| **In scope** | The tenth feature key, `analytics`, OFF with no row (D-134's shape). `tenants.analytics_id` (a GA4 measurement ID per tenant), refused by shape, required before the switch goes on, returned by `tenant_public()` ONLY while the switch is on (`sql/schema-analytics.sql`, the 46th file). The policy version bumped when the switch flips. `lib/analytics.ts` (pure: the stored choice, GPC/DNT, the address and referrer GA4 is given, the four step names) and `components/analytics.tsx` (the ConsentBar, the loader, `track()`), placed on S-1, S-6 and S-13 as Uma and Vera specified. The privacy page's analytics paragraphs and its AnalyticsChoice control. The Features tab's Analytics row with the ID field. The security headers of R-55 for the whole app, Google's hosts on the three measured paths only. verify checks, unit tests, a walk that intercepts every request to Google and lets none through, the GA property checklist, the record |
| **Out of scope** | Any staff page, `/platform`, `/`, `/privacy`, `/terms`, the tenant privacy and terms pages as measured pages (Q5 = no). Any analytics figure on S-11 (FR-023, Q2: owners read in GA4). Google's Consent Mode in any form (§ 2.2). The Measurement Protocol, Google Tag Manager, server-side tagging. Excluding signed-in staff (Q7 = no). Bot filtering beyond GA4's own. Removing `?ref=` from S-13's address bar (Uma's R-U5, a proposal to Rhea, not a requirement). A nonce CSP (§ 7 q4). Creating the GA4 properties and accepting Google's terms: the user's, by hand (§ 6.2) |

### What the user asked, and what the plan does with it

| The user's words | What exists today | What the plan does |
|---|---|---|
| "google analytics" (`todo.md:9`) | S-11 counts only guests who acted (D-098); nothing counts visits or sources | GA4 on S-1, S-6, S-13, per tenant, after consent |
| Gate 2: Q1 = A (GA4); Q2 default (owners read their own tenant, the operator reads all; admins and staff not) | No GA anywhere; no CSP (R-55) | ONE GA4 property per tenant (§ 1.2), so GA4's own access model gives an owner their tenant and nothing else |
| T-006: "Q8 is yours: can GA4 meet FR-analytics-011 to 014 and FR-analytics-006?" | A vendor fact nobody had read | § 1, answered: 006, 011, 012 yes; 013 yes with one word changed; 014 only if Rhea names GA4's own fields; and 022 forces a property per tenant |

---

## 0. The eight rules

### Rule 1: Nothing from Google before Allow

Nothing from Google is in the HTML: no `<script src>`, no inline `gtag`
stub, no `preconnect`. The ConsentBar decides on the device, after
hydration. Only an Allow (a click now, or a valid stored allow) runs
`loadAnalytics()`, which writes `window.dataLayer` and appends ONE `<script
src="https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=…">`. Consent Mode is NOT
used, basic or advanced: a default-denied consent command is itself Google
code running before a choice (Lex Q3.1). Declined, ignored, GPC, DNT,
unwritable storage, a 404, the switch off, no ID: the function is never
called. The walk proves it from the network log, not from reading the code.

### Rule 2: The app sends only what it wrote itself

- `config` gets exactly these settings, and nothing else:
  - `send_page_view: false`;
  - `page_location` from `measuredLocation()`;
  - `page_referrer` from `measuredReferrer()`;
  - `page_title`, one of three fixed words: Chat, Booking page, Manage booking;
  - `allow_google_signals: false` and `allow_ad_personalization_signals: false`;
  - `cookie_prefix` per tenant and `cookie_expires` of 180 days (§ 2.5).
- The page view is sent by the module.
- `track(step)` takes ONE argument, a `StepEvent`, the union `'chat_started' |
  'quote_shown' | 'request_sent' | 'stay_found'`. It has no parameter object,
  so no caller can attach a property. That is FR-analytics-014 held by the
  compiler.
- Nothing typed, spoken, priced, referenced or identified is in reach of the
  module. It is given the slug, the page, the ID and the step name, and
  nothing more.

### Rule 3: Two walls, each alone (D-038)

- **Wall 1, the code:** the page passes `analyticsId` to the client only if
  `flags.analytics` is on, and the module does nothing without an ID.
- **Wall 2, Postgres:** `tenant_public()` returns `analytics_id` as `null`
  while the switch is off, whatever the column holds. A trigger refuses to
  switch it on with no ID, and another refuses to clear the ID while the
  switch is on.
- verify proves wall 2 alone: the column is set, the switch is off, and
  `tenant_public()` gives null. The positive twin is the switch on, which
  gives the ID.
- A unit test proves wall 1 alone: the flag is off and an ID is passed, and
  nothing renders and nothing loads.

### Rule 4: Only the three pages, and they leave nothing behind

- The bar and the loader are rendered by `page.tsx` of S-1, S-6 and S-13, and
  only after their `notFound()` checks. The tenant layout is NOT the place
  (plan.md:678's seam is refused): the layout also wraps `/admin/**`, privacy
  and terms.
- Moving to an unmeasured page with a Next `<Link>` keeps the window and the
  loaded `gtag.js`. So the module sets `window['ga-disable-<ID>'] = true`
  when the measured page unmounts, and clears it when a measured page mounts
  with consent **[unverified]**.
- Every link from a measured page into `/t/<slug>/admin` is a plain `<a>`, a
  fresh document under the staff CSP. Today that is `public-footer.tsx`'s
  "Staff login" and `tenant-nav.tsx`'s staff link.
- The CSP (Rule 8) is the browser's wall: on every other path, Google's
  hosts are not allowed.

### Rule 5: A step is a success the screen already drew

Each step event fires where the screen has already drawn the success, and
only once:

| Event | Fires when | Fires at most |
|---|---|---|
| `chat_started` | `sawDone` on the first turn of a conversation, at the point where `conversationId` goes from null to a value | Once per conversation. "New chat" starts a new one |
| `quote_shown` | the quote state first holds a `RequestQuote` | Once per load |
| `request_sent` | `setSent()` | Once per accepted request |
| `stay_found` | `setStay()` with a stay | Once per load |

- A 429, 409, validation error, `error` event or network failure fires
  nothing, because those branches throw or return before the success line.
- Nothing is replayed after a late Allow (R-U6): the count means "steps
  taken after allowing".

### Rule 6: The choice is the guest's, kept on the device, per tenant

- localStorage key `analytics:<slug>`, value `{ choice: 'allow' | 'decline',
  at, version, via: 'bar' | 'privacy' }`.
- A choice is valid while it is under `ANALYTICS_CHOICE_DAYS` (180) old and
  its `version` equals the tenant's `policy_version`. Anything else is no
  choice.
- GPC (`navigator.globalPrivacyControl === true`) or DNT
  (`navigator.doNotTrack === '1'`) **[unverified: the property names]** is a
  Decline with no bar. Only an allow made on the privacy page (`via:
  'privacy'`) overrides the signal (Lex Q9).
- If storage cannot be written there is no bar and nothing loads.
- Declining deletes this tenant's GA cookies (the prefix, § 2.5). Nothing
  about the choice reaches the server (Lex Q3.1: no server log).

### Rule 7: The pages never wait on Google

- The loader is `async`, created after the choice.
- `gtag` failing to load, being blocked or answering slowly changes nothing a
  guest sees. There is no `onerror` UI, no retry and no `await` in any flow.
- `track()` returns `void` and never throws: it is wrapped, and a missing
  `window.gtag` is a no-op (FR-018).

### Rule 8: The security headers are this plan's, for every page (C4, BR-8, R-55)

- One pure function, `securityHeaders(pathname, env)` in `lib/csp.ts`, is
  unit-tested and applied by `middleware.ts`.
- **Every response gets:** HSTS, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`,
  `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `frame-ancestors
  'none'` (with `X-Frame-Options: DENY`), `Permissions-Policy` (microphone
  self only, for voice), and the base CSP.
- **Only the three measured path shapes** (`/t/<slug>`, `/t/<slug>/book`,
  `/t/<slug>/manage`) add Google's hosts.
- The chatbot is untouched: no prompt text, no tool text, and the three
  baselines are byte-identical at the end.

---

## 1. Q8 answered: can GA4 meet FR-analytics-006 and 011–014?

**Short answer.**
- **006, 011 and 012: yes, by construction.**
- **013: yes, with one word changed.**
- **014: only if Rhea names the fields GA4 sends by itself**, because no
  configuration removes them.
- **Two more FRs are touched:** 022 cannot be met with ONE property, which
  is why the plan uses one property per tenant, and 024 needs Lex's wording
  (GA4's shortest retention is 2 months, one figure per property).
- Each answer below rests on GA4 behaviour that is **[unverified]**. Phase 0
  reads it. If a fact is wrong, that FR's answer changes and Rhea is told;
  the FR does not relax.

### 1.1 FR by FR

| FR | Answer | How | Rests on |
|---|---|---|---|
| **006** Nothing before a choice | **Yes** | Rule 1: no Google code at all before Allow, so there is no Consent Mode and no ping. The walk checks the network log for zero requests to `*.google*.com` or `*.googletagmanager.com` before Allow, after Decline, with GPC, and with the switch off | Our code alone |
| **011** S-13 sends no query string | **Yes** | `page_location` = origin + `/t/<slug>/manage`, set before the first hit, with `send_page_view: false`. Enhanced measurement is OFF in the stream (§ 6.2), so gtag sends no history-change page view that reads `location` itself. `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` means the Referer HTTP header of the request to Google is the origin only | gtag uses `page_location` instead of `document.location` for `dl` **[unverified]**; the enhanced-measurement toggles exist **[unverified]** |
| **012** Only `utm_*` on S-1 and S-6 | **Yes** | `measuredLocation()` rebuilds the URL: origin, path, then the five `utm_*` keys in a fixed order, the first value each. Every other key and every fragment is dropped | GA4 reads campaign data from `page_location`'s `utm_*` **[unverified]** |
| **013** Referrer = an origin, never a path | **Yes, one word changed** | `measuredReferrer()` sets `page_referrer` on every hit. An external `document.referrer` gives its origin. An internal one, or the previous measured page after a client-side navigation (the module keeps it in memory, because `document.referrer` does not change on a `<Link>`), gives **our own origin**, which GA4 reads as "same site". None gives `''`, which gtag may refill from `document.referrer`. The FR says "the measured page's name or not at all": a page name is not a URL, and GA4 would count it as a referral from a site called "S-13". Our origin carries no path and no query, so it meets the FR's intent. **Rhea is asked to word it so** (M to rhea) | gtag uses `page_referrer` instead of `document.referrer` **[unverified]** |
| **014** A closed list of properties | **The app's side: yes. GA4's own fields: no configuration removes them** | Rule 2 closes what the app sends. GA4 adds, by itself, its client and session ids (the cookie the consent is about), the session count, engagement time, screen resolution, language, user-agent client hints, its consent and version flags, and a location it derives from the IP address. Granular location and device collection can be switched OFF in the property (§ 6.2), and Google says it stores no IP address. Each of these is **[unverified]**. The FR lists "device class and browser language the means records by itself". **Rhea is asked** to name GA4's own technical fields as allowed, or GA4 fails 014 as written. I do not relax it | Google's parameter reference **[unverified]** |
| *022* One tenant never reads another's | **Only with a property per tenant** | A GA4 property has no row-level access **[unverified]**: an owner who can view a shared property can view every tenant in it. So each tenant has its own property and measurement ID (FR-020's setting), in the operator's GA account. The operator sees all (US-3), and each owner is a Viewer on their own property only. Each property also has its own time zone (FR-021's "in the tenant's day") | GA4 access is per account or property **[unverified]** |
| *021* 7/30/90 days | **Yes** | Standard reports (pages, traffic acquisition, events) are aggregates. The 2-month retention setting limits explorations only **[unverified]**, so a 90-day view works in Reports, and Lex's 2 months stands (M-009 point 4) | **[unverified]** |
| *024* Retention bounded and stated | **Needs Rhea's rewording** | GA4 offers 2 or 14 months **[unverified]**. One figure per property, which can never follow a tenant's chat period. The plan sets 2 months and states it as a constant (`ANALYTICS_RETENTION_MONTHS`) on the privacy page, as Lex proposed | Lex Q3.4 |

### 1.2 Why one property per tenant, not one for the platform

- Lex's L-A3 and Uma's U-A2 assumed ONE platform property. FR-022 cannot be
  met that way for owners (§ 1.1), and a single property has a single time
  zone and a single retention setting.
- A property per tenant costs one text field and one column. Lex calls it
  legally the cleaner shape (Q3.6): each tenant's data sits in its own
  property, and the operator reading across tenants is the operator reading
  N properties it administers.
- Where the properties live (the operator's account, or each tenant's own)
  is the user's choice (§ 7 q1). The code is the same either way: one ID per
  tenant.
- Uma's U-A2 already designed this alternative ("§ 6.2 gains one text field
  beside the switch, refused by shape with a sentence"). Vera styles it from
  existing rules (M to uma and vera).

---

## 2. Traps

### 2.1 Every GA4 fact here is unread

- No Google page was read in this session (Context7 is unauthorised), so
  Phase 0 reads, through Context7 or Google's own pages:
  - the gtag `config` fields of Rule 2;
  - `ga-disable-<ID>`;
  - `cookie_prefix` and `cookie_expires`;
  - the enhanced-measurement and granular-data toggles;
  - the data-retention options and what they govern;
  - the property access model;
  - the CSP hosts Google lists for GA4;
  - the GA data processing terms.
- Each fact is recorded as confirmed or wrong in `plan/analytics/phase0.md`.
- A wrong fact stops the phase that needs it and goes to the owner of the FR
  it breaks. It is not patched around.

### 2.2 Consent Mode is a trap for this design

The standard snippet sets `gtag('consent', 'default', {…denied})` and loads
the tag at once. With "advanced" behaviour that sends cookieless pings
before any choice, which fails FR-006 (Lex Q3.1). "Basic" behaviour still
loads Google's script before the choice. This plan uses neither. The tag is
simply absent until Allow, so there is nothing to configure wrongly.

### 2.3 A `<Link>` keeps the tag

- Next's client-side navigation keeps `window`, `dataLayer` and the loaded
  `gtag.js`.
- If enhanced measurement's "page changes based on browser history events"
  were on, a `<Link>` from S-1 to `/t/villa/admin` would send `/admin` to
  Google.
- Three guards cover this:
  1. the toggle OFF (§ 6.2);
  2. `ga-disable-<ID>` when the measured page unmounts (Rule 4);
  3. staff links as plain `<a>`.
- The walk navigates S-1 → privacy → back → Staff login, and asserts zero
  hits after leaving S-1.

### 2.4 The CSP of the first document is the CSP of the whole session

- A CSP header applies to the document that loaded it. A client-side
  navigation keeps the first page's policy.
- So S-1's Google allowance would reach a privacy page opened with a `<Link>`.
  That is acceptable, because nothing loads there (Rule 4).
- It would also reach `/admin`, which is why staff links are `<a>`: the staff
  screens always start with the staff CSP.

### 2.5 Cookies are per host, tenants are per path

- Every tenant is on one host (`/t/villa`, `/t/alteza`), so GA's default
  `_ga` cookie would be ONE client id across tenants.
- A guest who allowed both would then be the same id in two tenants'
  properties. That id is per host, so it would not single out the person,
  but it breaks the per-tenant boundary.
- `cookie_prefix: 'ga_<slug>'` **[unverified]** gives each tenant its own
  cookies.
- Decline deletes the cookies with that prefix.
- `cookie_expires: 15552000` (180 days) **[unverified]** keeps GA's cookie
  inside the consent's life (Lex Q3.3).

### 2.6 `tenant_public()` is replaced for the fourth time (trap 20, trap 25)

- The 46th file drops and re-creates `tenant_public()` with `analytics_id`.
- `schema-welcome-text.sql` (the 44th) does the same with one column fewer,
  so its step 2 is guarded on `analytics_id` existing, exactly as
  `schema-legal.sql` was guarded on `welcome_text`.
- `schema-voice.sql` (the 41st) puts back a nine-key constraint and a
  `tenant_feature_on()` that knows only voice. A re-run after this file must
  skip both, so both are guarded on `analytics_id` existing.
- `audit_row()`'s `tenants` allowlist gains `analytics_id`. That is an edit
  to the 43rd file, so the 43rd and every file after it are re-run in order
  (trap 25).

### 2.7 Switching on changes the privacy text, so the version changes

- The analytics paragraphs appear and disappear with the switch (FR-019), so
  every flip is a new privacy text.
- Lex: bump `policy_version` when the switch goes on, which re-asks every
  stored choice and every booking consent (D-129).
- The 46th file's trigger does it in SQL, for every door (the platform
  route, a CLI, a hand):
  - a numeric version becomes n + 1, on an ON and on an OFF;
  - a non-numeric version (the check allows `v1.2`) is refused with a
    sentence: "Set the next policy version on the Legal tab before switching
    analytics."
- The `tenants` update writes its own audit row (`policy_version` is in the
  allowlist already).

### 2.8 The bar is decided after hydration, so it lands one frame late

- The server cannot read localStorage, so the server and the first client
  render show nothing, and an effect decides.
- On S-6 and S-13 the bar is inserted above `<main>` one frame after the
  first paint. Uma's M-012 point 1 asked if that is acceptable: **yes**. It
  lands before any field could hold focus, and a reserved slot would be a
  permanent empty gap for every guest who has already chosen (Vera: "no
  empty slot when hidden").
- The `role="status"` line is server-rendered and empty, outside the bar
  (Vera § 3.1).

### 2.9 A walk that sends real hits sends real data

- The walk never lets a request reach Google. Playwright routes
  `**/*google-analytics.com/**` and `**/*analytics.google.com/**`, records
  each request's URL and body, then aborts it.
- `gtag.js` itself is fetched from `www.googletagmanager.com`, a free GET.
  If it will not load for a test ID, the walk needs the user's walk
  property's ID (§ 7 q5).
- The recorded payloads are AC-11's and AC-15's "raw events". The walk
  greps them for the PII strings it typed, and for every key outside the
  allowlist.

### 2.10 Development and the CSP

- `next dev` needs `'unsafe-eval'` for its refresh runtime, so
  `securityHeaders()` adds it in development only, and the unit test pins
  that production has none.
- A Vercel PREVIEW deployment's toolbar (`vercel.live`) is blocked by the
  production CSP. That is accepted, and recorded in R-55.

---

## 3. The data model

`packages/db/sql/schema-analytics.sql`, the 46th file. It runs in one
transaction and is idempotent. It is re-run in order after the 45th (§ 2.6).

```sql
-- 1. The tenth key, and no row = OFF for analytics as for voice.
alter table public.tenant_features drop constraint if exists tenant_features_key;
alter table public.tenant_features add  constraint tenant_features_key check (feature in (
  'dashboard','conversations','unanswered','suggested_questions',
  'booking_page','manage_booking','calendar','notifications','voice','analytics'));
create or replace function public.tenant_feature_on(p_tenant_id bigint, p_feature text) returns boolean
language sql stable set search_path = '' as $$
  select coalesce((select f.enabled from public.tenant_features f
                   where f.tenant_id = p_tenant_id and f.feature = p_feature),
                  p_feature not in ('voice','analytics'))
$$;   -- grants as schema-voice.sql

-- 2. The measurement ID. Public by nature (it is in every hit), but handed out only while on (step 5).
alter table public.tenants add column if not exists analytics_id text;
alter table public.tenants drop constraint if exists tenants_analytics_id_shape;
alter table public.tenants add  constraint tenants_analytics_id_shape
  check (analytics_id is null or analytics_id ~ '^G-[A-Z0-9]{6,12}$');   -- the length is Phase 0's to confirm

-- 3. On needs an ID; an ID cannot go while on. check_violation (23514), in words, so every
--    door maps it to a 400 (lib/route.ts, fromPostgrest()).
--    tenant_features BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE, feature = 'analytics' and new.enabled:
--      no analytics_id → 'Set the Google Analytics measurement ID before switching analytics on.'
--    tenants BEFORE UPDATE OF analytics_id, new null and tenant_feature_on(id,'analytics'):
--      → 'Switch analytics off before removing its measurement ID.'

-- 4. Every flip bumps policy_version (§ 2.7). tenant_features AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF enabled,
--    feature = 'analytics', enabled changed (an insert of enabled = false from no row is no change):
--      numeric → (n + 1)::text; otherwise raise check_violation with the Legal-tab sentence.
--    security invoker: the super token can update tenants already (the platform form does);
--    set search_path = '', every name qualified (trap 19).

-- 5. tenant_public(), with analytics_id, NULL unless the switch is on (Rule 3, wall 2).
--    drop + create (the return type changes), the same body as the 44th file plus:
--      case when public.tenant_feature_on(t.id, 'analytics') then t.analytics_id end as analytics_id
--    still security definer, search_path = '', no archived tenant; grants re-applied.
```

**Edits to older files (guards, trap 20).**
- **`schema-voice.sql`:** both statements are guarded on
  `tenants.analytics_id` existing, so a re-run is a no-op once the 46th has
  run.
- **`schema-welcome-text.sql`:** step 2 is guarded the same way.
- **`schema-audit-log.sql`:** `audit_row()`'s `tenants` `v_keep` gains
  `'analytics_id'`.
- After these edits, the 43rd, 44th, 45th and 46th files are re-applied in
  that order.

**Not a definer, not a new table, no new policy.** `tenant_features`
policies are unchanged (super users write, each tenant reads its own). The
audit trigger already covers `tenant_features` (FR-025: "turned analytics
on" by whom and when) and `tenants`. CLAUDE.md rule 8's lists do not grow.

---

## 4. The modules and the contracts

### 4.1 Server side (no new route)

- **`@rag/pipeline` tenant:** `TenantContext` gains `analyticsId: string |
  null` from `tenant_public()`.
- **The platform route:** the existing `PATCH /api/platform/tenants/[id]`
  (`withPlatformRoute()`) gains `analyticsId` in `lib/schemas.ts`, a string
  matching the shape above or null, trimmed and upper-cased.
  - 400 with the check's words on a bad shape.
  - 400 with the trigger's words on clearing the ID while the switch is on.
- **The switch:** the existing feature route (`/applications/…` sibling,
  `features-panel.tsx`'s `send()`) is unchanged. Switching on with no ID is
  the trigger's 400, shown in the panel's existing refusal toast.
- **`lib/features.ts`:** a tenth entry, `{ key: 'analytics', label:
  'Analytics', group: 'Guest pages', defaultOn: false, about: 'Counts visits
  on the chat, booking page and Manage booking with Google Analytics, after
  each guest allows it.' }` (Vera § 8). The key is in both lists (§ 3 step
  1), and `featureFlags({}).analytics === false`.
- **The three pages:** each passes `analytics={nav.flags.analytics &&
  tenant.analyticsId ? { id, slug, page, policyVersion } : null}` to its
  Client Component, after every `notFound()`.
  - `page` is `'chat' | 'book' | 'manage'`.
  - The prop is a plain object, never the context.
- **The privacy page:** passes the same prop to `AnalyticsChoice`, and
  `analytics: true` into `tenantPrivacy()`.
- **No API route sends or receives an analytics event** (FR-003: none is
  measured). Nothing in `app/api/**` changes for this, except the platform
  PATCH's schema.

### 4.2 `apps/web/lib/analytics.ts` (pure, browser-safe, tested)

```ts
export const ANALYTICS_CHOICE_DAYS = 180;           // Lex Q3.3
export const ANALYTICS_RETENTION_MONTHS = 2;        // Lex Q3.4; the property setting, § 6.2
export const GA_COOKIE_SECONDS = ANALYTICS_CHOICE_DAYS * 86_400;
export type MeasuredPage = 'chat' | 'book' | 'manage';
export type StepEvent = 'chat_started' | 'quote_shown' | 'request_sent' | 'stay_found';
export const PAGE_TITLE: Record<MeasuredPage, string> = { chat: 'Chat', book: 'Booking page', manage: 'Manage booking' };
export interface StoredChoice { choice: 'allow' | 'decline'; at: string; version: string; via: 'bar' | 'privacy' }
export function choiceKey(slug: string): string;                                   // 'analytics:<slug>'
export function readChoice(raw: string | null, version: string, now: Date): StoredChoice | null;  // expired / other version / malformed → null
export function privacySignal(nav: { globalPrivacyControl?: boolean; doNotTrack?: string | null }): boolean;
export function decide(stored: StoredChoice | null, signal: boolean, writable: boolean): 'load' | 'ask' | 'none';
export function measuredLocation(href: string, page: MeasuredPage): string;          // S-13: origin + path, nothing else
export function measuredReferrer(referrer: string, origin: string, previousPage: MeasuredPage | null): string;  // external → its origin; else our origin
export function cookiePrefix(slug: string): string;                                 // 'ga_' + slug, [a-z0-9_] only
```

- `decide()` returns `'none'` for any signal unless `stored.via ===
  'privacy' && stored.choice === 'allow'`.
- `decide()` returns `'none'` for unwritable storage.
- `decide()` returns `'load'` for a valid allow, `'none'` for a valid
  decline, and `'ask'` otherwise.

### 4.3 `apps/web/components/analytics.tsx` (Client)

- **`<AnalyticsRoot analytics={…|null}>`** is a context provider placed by
  each Client Screen. With `null` it renders its children and nothing else,
  and `track()` is a no-op.
- **`useAnalytics()`** returns `{ track(step: StepEvent): void }`, which is
  all a screen sees.
- **`<ConsentBar />`** is Vera § 3.1's markup, exactly, with the polite
  status `<p>` as a sibling outside the section.
  - S-1 renders it inside `.composer`, after `.jump-down` and before
    `VoiceStatus`.
  - S-6 and S-13 render it as `<div class="consent-slot">` between
    `{header}` and `<main className="book-main" tabIndex={-1}>`, only when
    shown.
  - After an answer, focus goes to the input on S-1 and to `<main>` on S-6
    and S-13, and only if focus was on a bar button (Uma § 5.3).
- **`loadAnalytics(id, page, slug)`** runs once per document, guarded by a
  module flag:
  - it sets `window.dataLayer` and `window.gtag`;
  - then `gtag('js', new Date())` and `gtag('config', id, {…Rule 2})`;
  - then appends the async script.
  - Each later measured-page mount (a `<Link>` within the tenant) clears
    `ga-disable-<id>`, updates `page_location`, `page_referrer` and
    `page_title` with `gtag('set', …)`, and sends `gtag('event',
    'page_view')` once (FR-015).
  - Unmount sets `ga-disable-<id>`.
- **`clearAnalyticsCookies(slug)`** expires every cookie whose name starts
  with `cookiePrefix(slug)`, on the path `/` and the host.
- **`<AnalyticsChoice />`** is the privacy section's control: the five
  states and "just changed" (Uma F-2, Vera § 6.2). It writes `via:
  'privacy'`, and Decline also clears the cookies.

### 4.4 The screens' four lines

- **`chat-screen.tsx`:** after `if (!sawDone) throw …`, if
  `firstTurnOfConversation`, then `track('chat_started')`. A `useRef`
  records the conversation id it fired for.
- **`booking-page.tsx`:**
  - `track('quote_shown')` the first time `quote.quote` becomes non-null
    (an effect with a ref);
  - `track('request_sent')` after `setSent()`.
- **`manage-booking.tsx`:** `track('stay_found')` after `setStay(body.stay)`,
  once per load.
- **`public-footer.tsx` "Staff login" and `tenant-nav.tsx`'s staff link:**
  `<a>`, not `<Link>` (Rule 4).

### 4.5 The privacy text (`lib/legal.ts`)

- `TenantLegalFacts` gains `analytics?: boolean`.
- When true, Lex Q3.5's five placeholder texts go in, built from the two
  constants and `businessName`, never retyped. They are Rhea's to adopt
  under FR-019 and a lawyer's to replace (R-60):
  - "What is collected" replaces line 95's sentence;
  - "Why it is used" gains a paragraph;
  - "Who it is shared with" gains the Google line before "Nobody else";
  - "How long it is kept" gains the line;
  - a new section "Your analytics choice" is added, with `id: 'analytics'`,
    after "How long it is kept".
- When false, line 95 stays word for word (AC-19). A test pins both.
- `LegalSection` gains an optional `id`. `LegalBody` renders `id` on the
  section's `h2`, and the privacy page passes a `controls` map `{ analytics:
  <AnalyticsChoice …/> }` that `LegalBody` draws after that section's
  paragraphs. This is Uma's R-U7, M-012 point 3: feasible, and the page
  stays a Server Component.
- `platformPrivacy()` is unchanged ("This landing page … uses no
  analytics" stays true, Q5).

### 4.6 The platform form

- The Features tab's Analytics row (Vera § 8) gains one field under it:
  "Google Analytics measurement ID", a native text input with a Save button
  of its own (it PATCHes the tenant; the switch beside it still saves at
  once, D-V2).
- With no saved ID, the switch is `disabled`, with the visible sentence "Set
  the measurement ID first." (D-102: text, no `title`).
- Activity rows: `activityWords` gains "turned Analytics on/off" (the
  feature row) and "changed the Analytics measurement ID" (the tenants
  column), for FR-025.

### 4.7 The headers (`lib/csp.ts`, `apps/web/middleware.ts`)

```
base (every path):
  default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline';
  img-src 'self' data: blob: <SUPABASE_URL origin>; connect-src 'self'; media-src 'self' blob:;
  font-src 'self'; worker-src 'self'; manifest-src 'self'; object-src 'none';
  base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'
measured paths (^/t/[^/]+(/book|/manage)?/?$) add:
  script-src https://www.googletagmanager.com
  connect-src https://*.google-analytics.com https://*.analytics.google.com https://*.googletagmanager.com
  img-src     https://*.google-analytics.com https://*.googletagmanager.com      [the hosts: unverified, Phase 0]
development adds script-src 'unsafe-eval' (§ 2.10).
```

- **`'unsafe-inline'` in `script-src`:** Next's App Router writes inline RSC
  scripts, and without a nonce they need it. What this CSP still walls off
  is every foreign script host and every foreign connect destination. A
  nonce CSP is the stronger step (§ 7 q4).
- **`'unsafe-inline'` in `style-src`:** R-55's note was wrong on this point.
  An inline `style` ATTRIBUTE in server-rendered HTML (the tenant theme's
  custom properties, D-030) is blocked by a CSP without it **[to confirm in
  Phase 5's browser run]**.
- The middleware matcher excludes `_next/static`, `_next/image` and
  `favicon.ico`.
- `securityHeaders()` is pure and table-tested on: `/t/villa`,
  `/t/villa/book`, `/t/villa/manage`, `/t/villa/manage/`, `/t/villa/admin`,
  `/t/villa/privacy`, `/t/villa/book/x`, `/platform`, `/`, `/api/t/villa/chat`
  and `/t/villa/sw.js`.
- **The service worker's own scope:** `worker-src 'self'` covers `/t/<slug>/sw.js`.

---

## 5. Phases

Each phase ends with its checks green and is recorded in `status.md` and
`whats-done.md` (the house's way). The branch is `feat/analytics`, from a
clean `master`.

### Phase 0: Baseline, and the vendor read

- Record the baselines:
  - web tests and typecheck;
  - verify 243 and rooms 57;
  - the three chatbot baselines diffed (`--strip-trailing-cr`).
- Pipeline and bookings isolation cannot run (northwind and harbor are
  deleted), which is recorded as such. The battery is not run (Rule 8: the
  chatbot is untouched).
- **The vendor read** (§ 2.1), through Context7 or Google's pages, needs `/mcp`
  authorised. Each [unverified] line of § 1 and § 4 is recorded as confirmed
  or wrong in `plan/analytics/phase0.md`.
- **Check:** every row has a source. A wrong fact goes to its FR's owner, and
  the phases after it wait.

### Phase 1: SQL (`schema-analytics.sql` and the three guards)

- Apply it the record's way: Claude on `DATABASE_URL`, then 43 → 46 in order.
- verify gains 244–250:
  - **244:** with no row, `tenant_feature_on(villa,'analytics')` is false,
    and voice is still false with no row.
  - **245:** a bad ID shape is refused (23514), and a good one is stored
    upper-case.
  - **246:** switching on with no ID is refused in the trigger's words, and
    clearing the ID while on is refused.
  - **247:** wall 2 alone: the ID is set and the switch is off, and an anon
    or chat `tenant_public('villa')` gives `analytics_id` null. The positive
    twin is the switch on, which gives the ID.
  - **248:** a flip bumps a numeric `policy_version` by one, each way, and a
    non-numeric version refuses the flip.
  - **249:** a staff token and a chat token cannot write `tenant_features`.
  - **250:** the audit rows: the feature row and `analytics_id` change each
    write one, with the actor.
- The test tenant is restored by ids (trap 26): version, ID and row.
- verify 250, rooms 57.

### Phase 2: The pure module and the headers function

- `lib/analytics.ts` and `lib/analytics.test.ts`:
  - `readChoice`: 179 and 181 days, the other version, malformed JSON;
  - `decide`: every combination of the three inputs;
  - `measuredLocation`: AC-12's URL gives exactly the path; AC-13's keeps
    two `utm_*` and drops `foo` and `#z`; a repeated `utm` key gives the
    first value;
  - `measuredReferrer`: AC-14's two cases, plus `''` and a malformed URL;
  - `cookiePrefix` on odd slugs.
- `lib/csp.ts` and `lib/csp.test.ts`: § 4.7's table, and production with no
  `unsafe-eval`.
- `features.ts` gains its tenth entry, and its test pins
  `featureFlags({}).analytics === false`.
- `legal.ts` gains the analytics text, and its test pins line 95 when off
  and the five texts when on.
- **Check:** web tests and typecheck.

### Phase 3: The client module, the bar, the four steps, the privacy control

- Build § 4.3–4.5.
- Component tests on a fake `window`:
  - wall 1 alone: the flag is off and an ID is passed, and nothing renders
    and no script is appended;
  - `track()` with no gtag is a no-op;
  - a second mount loads no second script;
  - unmount sets `ga-disable`.
- The chat's `chat_started` fires once per conversation: a fake stream, two
  turns, then New chat, gives 2.
- The staff links are `<a>`. A test greps `public-footer.tsx` and
  `tenant-nav.tsx` for a `<Link` to `/admin`.
- Vera's CSS goes into `screens.css` and `chat.css` (the 760 selector list,
  the `.book-main` rule, `.book-main:focus`). No literal, no dark rule.

### Phase 4: The platform form, and TenantContext

- Build § 4.1, § 4.6 and the activity words.
- `plan/tenant-management-phase4-walk.mjs` gains three checks: the PATCH
  shape, switch on without an ID gives 400 in words, and off then on gives
  two Activity rows. It runs on a throwaway tenant made and removed by id.

### Phase 5: The headers on every page

- Apply `middleware.ts`.
- `plan/csp-walk.mjs` (new) opens, in Chromium, each page the a11y walks
  already list (`plan/ui-refresh-a11y.mjs`'s states). It collects every
  `securitypolicyviolation` event and every console CSP error. Expect **0**.
- It also reads each response's headers, and expects:
  - Google's hosts on the three measured shapes only;
  - `frame-ancestors 'none'` everywhere.
- The existing a11y walks stay at 0 violations.
- **Check:** the walk's count, recorded. R-55's style-attribute note is
  confirmed or corrected from the run.

### Phase 6: The analytics walk (the network is the evidence)

`plan/analytics-walk.mjs` runs against `pnpm dev`, on villa with a throwaway
measurement ID or the walk property (§ 7 q5). Google's collect endpoints
are intercepted and aborted (§ 2.9), and villa's flag, ID and
`policy_version` are restored by id at the end. Its checks, numbered by AC:

1. **AC-01, AC-05.** The switch is off. S-1, S-6 and S-13 make 0 requests to
   Google hosts, and no `ga_villa*` cookie is set.
2. **AC-06.** The switch is on, in a fresh profile. Before an answer there
   are 0 Google requests and no cookie.
3. **AC-07.** Decline, then chat, quote, request and lookup: all succeed,
   with 0 Google requests.
4. **AC-08.** With the bar unanswered, the chat, the form and the lookup are
   completed by keyboard alone. The two buttons' boxes are equal.
5. **AC-09.** Allow on villa, then alteza (switch on, its own ID) shows its
   own bar. Decline on villa's privacy page, and the next villa load sends 0.
6. **AC-10.** The D-129 box is unticked and required after Allow.
7. **AC-11, AC-15.** A chat with a name, a mobile number and an email; a
   request with a promo code and a note; a lookup by reference. Every
   intercepted payload contains none of those strings, no reference, no
   uuid and no peso amount. Every `ep.*` and `up.*` key, and every app-set
   field, is in the allowlist.
8. **AC-12, AC-13, AC-14.** The `dl` and `dr` of the hits, as specified.
9. **AC-16, AC-17.** One `page_view` per load. `chat_started` 1 then 0. A
   first message answered 429 (a fresh `X-Forwarded-For`, 31 turns: D-137)
   gives 0, then a success gives 1. A 409 gives no `request_sent`, a miss no
   `stay_found`, a hit 1.
10. **AC-18.** Google is blocked (routes fail). The chat, quote, request and
    lookup give the same results as with the switch off, and no error is
    drawn.
11. **AC-03, § 2.3.** After Allow, follow privacy → back → Staff login: 0
    hits after leaving S-1, and the admin document has no googletagmanager
    script.
12. **AC-04.** `/t/no-such`, an archived tenant and `/book` with
    `booking_page` off: 404, 0 Google requests.
13. **GPC.** A context with `globalPrivacyControl` gives no bar and 0
    requests. "Allow analytics anyway" on privacy then loads on the next S-1.
14. **AC-19.** Villa's privacy page names Google. Alteza's (switch off) keeps
    line 95 word for word.
15. **Vera § 9.7.** `.consent-bar` height at 375×667 with a touch context, on
    S-1, with villa's and alteza's names, recorded (pass ≤ 120 px).
    Horizontal scroll at 320 and at 200 % zoom. Axe over the bar on S-1, S-6
    and S-13 × light, dark and pinned light, and over the privacy control's
    states: 0 violations.

Plus verify 250, rooms 57, web tests, typecheck, the three baselines
byte-identical, and the `.next/static` grep (CLAUDE.md rule 2).

### Phase 7: The record

- **D-151** is amended from "proposed" to what was built.
- **Risks:**
  - R-55 is **closed, or amended** with the nonce step left (q4);
  - R-63 is amended with Phase 0's findings;
  - R-60 notes the analytics placeholders.
- **CLAUDE.md:** the header paragraph, 46 SQL files, verify 250, the layout
  lines (`lib/analytics.ts`, `components/analytics.tsx`, `lib/csp.ts`,
  `middleware.ts`), and the features list (ten).
- `status.md`, `whats-done.md`, and the GA property checklist (§ 6.2) in
  R-61's deploy list.
- **Owed after the record, by the user:**
  - creating the properties, following § 6.2;
  - Google's terms;
  - a lawyer's reading (Lex § 6);
  - Rhea's FR wording (M to rhea).
- No real guest is measured before these are done (BR-7, Lex § 5).

---

## 6. What must not change

### 6.1 The product

- **The chatbot:** no prompt text, no tool text, no `dates.ts` or
  `language.ts` line. The three baselines are byte-identical.
- **S-11 and the Pulse strip:** no figure added, and no source changed
  (FR-023).
- **The D-129 booking consent box:** its words, place and requirement are
  unchanged (FR-009).
- **The voice notice and the chat's fine print** keep their words. `/`,
  `/privacy` and `/terms` keep theirs too.
- **The tenant privacy page with the switch off:** word for word.
- **No `service_role` in a request**, no new definer function and no new
  policy.
- **Every staff page and `/platform`:** no analytics code, and no Google host
  in their CSP.

### 6.2 The GA property checklist (the user, by hand, before a real guest)

For each tenant's property **[every setting name unverified, Phase 0]**:

- time zone Asia/Manila;
- data retention 2 months;
- Google signals OFF;
- ads personalisation OFF;
- every data-sharing setting OFF;
- every enhanced-measurement toggle OFF (page changes on history events,
  scrolls, outbound clicks, site search, form interactions, video, file
  downloads);
- granular location and device data collection OFF;
- user-provided data collection OFF;
- Google's GA data processing terms accepted (Lex M-009 point 6);
- each owner a Viewer on their own property only;
- no other property linked.

The measurement ID goes on the platform form. This checklist joins R-61.

---

## 7. Questions, each with a recommendation

1. **Where the properties live.** **Recommend** a property per tenant in the
   operator's GA account, with owners granted Viewer on theirs. That meets
   FR-021, FR-022 and US-3 with GA4's own access model, and Lex calls a
   per-tenant property the cleaner shape (Q3.6). The alternative is each
   tenant's own Google account, where the tenant is plainly the controller
   and the operator loses the cross-tenant view unless granted. The code is
   identical either way. One platform property is **not recommended**: it
   fails FR-022 for owners.
2. **Lex's controller FR**, "switch on only on the tenant's recorded written
   instruction" (M-009 point 8, Q3.6), is not yet an FR. **Recommend**
   Rhea adopt it, and then the 46th file gains `tenants.analytics_instructed_on
   date` (shown and set on the Legal tab like `dpa_signed_on`). Step 3's
   trigger then refuses ON without it, and Vera's "[if FR]" disabled switch
   applies. It adds one column and one condition. Until it is adopted it is
   not built.
3. **The [if FR] items Uma and Vera designed** (180 days, a version
   mismatch as no choice, GPC/DNT as Decline). **Recommend** building them
   as written (Rule 6). They only reduce what is collected, Lex advised
   them, and the UX and design already draw them. Rhea is asked to write
   them as FRs.
4. **The CSP's script wall.** **Recommend** the host-allowlist CSP of § 4.7
   now (`'unsafe-inline'` scripts, no nonce). It keeps `/` static, needs no
   per-request nonce plumbing, and still refuses every foreign script host
   and connect destination. A nonce with `'strict-dynamic'` is the stronger
   wall against an injected inline script. It makes every page dynamic, `/`
   included, and is left open in R-55 as a later plan.
5. **The walk's measurement ID.** **Recommend** a separate GA4 property
   named for the walk, in the operator's account, never a tenant's. The walk
   aborts every hit anyway (§ 2.9). It is needed only if `gtag.js` refuses
   to load for a made-up ID (Phase 0 finds out).
6. **Staff testing the public pages inflate the counts (Q7 = no).** Nothing
   is built. Staff can decline the bar like anyone. Recorded as a known
   inflation in R-63.
7. **The 319 px breakpoint (Vera § 3.2).** **Keep it.** It is Uma's
   "below 320 px, one per row" rule (UX § 8.7), and it costs one line.

# Decisions — RAG Chatbot POC

A running log. Each entry: what was decided, why, and what would change it.
Referenced from the other docs as `D-00n`.

**The decision behind all the others:** this is a **learning project**. The
stated goal is *"I want to fully understand how it works."* Where two options
compete, the one that makes the mechanism visible wins — even if it means more
code. Convenience that hides a step is a cost here, not a benefit.

---

## D-001 · No RAG framework · **Settled**

**Decision:** No LangChain, LlamaIndex, Vercel AI SDK, or Supabase AI helpers.
Chunking, embedding, retrieval and prompt assembly are all written by hand.

**Why:** These libraries exist to hide exactly the four steps the project is
built to expose. `RetrievalQAChain.fromLLM(...)` is one line and teaches nothing.
The hand-written version is roughly 60 lines and teaches the whole subject.

**Reverse if:** the project graduates into a real product where velocity matters
more than comprehension. By then the tradeoff will be an informed one.

---

## D-002 · Raw `fetch` instead of the `openai` SDK · **Settled**

**Decision:** Call `https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings` and
`/v1/chat/completions` directly with Node's built-in `fetch`.

**Why:** Requires Node 18+, which is a given. The two calls are ~10 lines each,
and writing them means seeing the actual request body — the `model`, `input`,
`messages` array, the shape of the response. The SDK would turn the two most
instructive HTTP requests in the project into opaque method calls.

Side benefit: one fewer dependency, and no SDK version churn to track.

**Reverse if:** you need streaming with retries and backoff, where the SDK's
handling is genuinely better than hand-rolled. That is post-MVP.

## D-003 · pgvector in Supabase, not a dedicated vector database · **Settled**

**Decision:** Embeddings live in a `vector(1536)` column in the same Postgres
database as the text.

**Why:** Supabase was a given. It ships pgvector on the free tier. A separate
vector DB (Pinecone, Chroma, Qdrant, Weaviate) would mean a second service to
run, a second set of credentials, and chunk text and chunk embedding split
across two systems that can drift out of sync. At this corpus size there is no
performance argument for it whatsoever.

**Reverse if:** millions of vectors, which this will never have.

## D-004 · `text-embedding-3-small`, 1536 dimensions · **Settled**

**Decision:** `text-embedding-3-small` for both ingestion and queries.

**Why:** OpenAI's cheapest current embedding model, and far more accurate than
needed for a handful of documents. 1536 dimensions is under pgvector's 2000-dim
limit for indexed columns, so the HNSW index works with no dimension-reduction
tricks.

**The two hard consequences — both are traps:**

1. **The same model must embed both the documents and the questions.** Different
   models produce vectors in unrelated coordinate spaces. Comparing across them
   yields plausible-looking similarity scores that are meaningless, and *nothing
   errors*. This is the most common silent RAG bug.
2. **Changing the model means changing `vector(1536)` and re-embedding every
   existing chunk.** Old vectors cannot be converted. Budget for a full
   re-ingest if you ever switch.

Verify current model names and pricing at
<https://platform.openai.com/docs/models> before building — this was written
2026-09-20 and model lineups move.

## D-005 · `gpt-4o-mini` for chat, set via env var · **Settled (the env var), soft (the model)**

**Decision:** Default `OPENAI_CHAT_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini`, read from `.env`.

**Why:** Cheap, fast, and entirely capable of "answer using only this context" —
that task is comprehension, not reasoning, so a frontier model buys nothing
here. Putting it in an env var means swapping models is a config change and a
restart, which makes comparing models a 30-second experiment instead of a code
edit.

**Soft part:** the specific model. Check the current OpenAI model list before
Phase 0 — if there is a newer small model, use it. Nothing in the code depends
on which model it is.

**Before production, decide this from measurement, not from instinct.** Run
`npm run eval` (the battery in `tools/prompt-eval.js`, with its cases rewritten
to use your own documents' facts) against each candidate model. Measured on this
build: `gpt-4o-mini` **5/6**, `gpt-4o` **6/6** on an identical prompt at roughly
**16× the input cost**, and the single case that separated them was applying a
general rule where the document also stated an exception. If your documents
contain carve-outs — pricing tiers, policy exceptions, eligibility bands — test
both. If they do not, the cheap model is very likely enough. See D-017 and the
production checklist in `README.md`.

## D-006 · `service_role` key, no RLS · **Superseded 2026-09-26 by D-038 and D-039**

> **Superseded.** Requests no longer use `service_role`: they reach Postgres
> on a tenant token under RLS policies (D-039), with the code filters kept as
> a second wall (D-038). `service_role` remains, at `@rag/db/service`, for
> tools only. The original decision is kept below as the record of why it
> was right for a one-user local POC.

**Decision:** The Express server uses Supabase's `service_role` key. No Row
Level Security policies are written.

**Why:** There is one user, no auth, and everything is localhost. The server is
the only client of the database, and it is trusted. Writing RLS policies for a
single-user local POC is ceremony that protects nothing.

**This is a deliberate, scoped shortcut, and it has an expiry date.** The
`service_role` key bypasses RLS entirely and must never reach the browser. See
`risks.md` § R-2.

**Reverse the moment** this is deployed anywhere public or gains a second user.
At that point RLS is mandatory, not optional.

**Amended 2026-09-20 during Phase 0.5.** Supabase's SQL editor warns when
`create table` runs without RLS, so `schema.sql` now enables RLS on all four
tables explicitly. The decision above is unchanged in substance: **no policies
are written.** RLS on with zero policies means `anon` and `authenticated` can do
nothing, while `service_role` — the only key the server holds — bypasses RLS and
is unaffected. This costs the POC nothing and retires the "the shortcut travels"
half of R-2 immediately rather than at first deploy. Writing actual policies is
still out of scope and still arrives with auth.

**Amended 2026-09-23, tenancy.** The reasoning above was "the server is the only
client of the database, and it is trusted". That is still true. What changed is
who the server serves: several tenants who do not trust each other (D-025). The
`service_role` key bypasses RLS for every one of their reads, so the thing that
keeps tenant A out of tenant B's rows is no longer the network. It is a
`tenant_id` filter in application code and inside two SQL functions. The weak
point of this posture has moved from "is the database reachable" to "did every
query remember its filter". The composite foreign keys cover writes; reads are
covered only by the leak cases and `tools/isolation.mjs`. See `risks.md` § R-11.
Writing real policies is still the fix, and it is now more urgent, not less.

## D-007 · Fixed-size chunking with overlap · **Settled for the MVP**

**Decision:** ~1000 characters per chunk, ~150 characters of overlap. Split on
character count, not tokens, sentences or semantics.

**Why:** It is the simplest thing that works, it is ~15 lines you can read in
one go, and it performs perfectly well on a small corpus. Smarter chunkers
(recursive, semantic, token-aware) are a meaningful improvement at scale — but
starting with them means never developing intuition for *why* they are better.

Phase 5 of the roadmap is specifically about changing these two numbers and
feeling the effect. That experiment only works if the baseline is naive.

**Superseded in part by D-018 (2026-09-20).** Phase 5 was run, the effect was
felt, and chunking moved retrieval quality more than any other knob — so the
splitter is now paragraph-aware. The sizes (1000 / 150) are unchanged and the
fixed-size sliding window survives as the fallback for oversized paragraphs and
for text with no blank lines. The "start naive" reasoning above still stands as
the reason it was done in this order.

**Characters, not tokens:** counting tokens requires a tokenizer dependency
(`tiktoken`/`gpt-tokenizer`) and buys precision the POC does not need. Roughly
4 characters ≈ 1 token for English is close enough for sizing.

## D-008 · Similarity threshold, with a short circuit · **Settled, value provisional**

**Decision:** `match_chunks` takes `min_similarity`, default `0.3`. When nothing
clears it, the server returns "I don't know based on the documents I have."
**without calling OpenAI at all.**

**Why:** Without a floor, vector search always returns its `match_count` nearest
chunks — including for a question completely unrelated to your corpus. Those
chunks then get pasted into the prompt as if they were relevant, and the model
does its best with irrelevant context. The threshold is what turns "always
answers" into "answers when it knows."

Skipping the OpenAI call is faster, free, and eliminates any chance of the model
ignoring the refusal instruction.

**Provisional:** `0.3` is a starting guess. Phase 3.2 of the roadmap is to log
real similarity scores on real questions and tune it. Too high and it refuses
things it knows; too low and it hallucinates from noise.

**Amended 2026-09-24 by D-035 (bookings Phase 6).** For a tenant with **no
tools**, nothing changed: zero chunks still means the refusal, with no OpenAI
call. `tool-leak` measured 0 answer calls for Northwind. For a tenant **with
tools**, the short circuit would have made the tool unreachable, because "is
the 12th free?" can match no document. So the model IS called with zero
chunks, and its reply is accepted only if it called a tool on that turn.
Otherwise the reply is replaced with the refusal. The guarantee D-008 exists
for (never an answer from training data when nothing was retrieved) still
holds. What is lost, for tool tenants only, is "free": a zero-match question
cost 485 in + 11 out, measured on "What is the capital of France?" asked of
villa.

## D-011 · Conversation history capped at ~6 messages · **Settled**

**Decision:** Send at most the last 6 messages with each request.

## D-015 · Hybrid search (vector + Postgres full-text), fused with RRF · **Post-MVP, added 2026-09-20**

**Decision:** Retrieval runs `match_chunks` (cosine) and `match_chunks_fts`
(Postgres full-text) in parallel and merges them with **Reciprocal Rank
Fusion**. Keyword hits are **not** subject to `MIN_SIMILARITY`.

**Why:** Phase 5 measured the weakness directly. `"extension 4417"` scored
**0.284** — worse than a vague paraphrase at 0.401 — because embeddings encode
meaning and an identifier has almost none. The originally planned threshold of
0.30 sat *above* that score, so the as-designed system would have refused a
question the documents answer.

**Why fuse by rank, not by score.** Cosine similarity and `ts_rank` are not
comparable: different scales, different distributions, and a "good" `ts_rank`
depends on the document. Averaging them or weighting them 70/30 means inventing
an exchange rate between two currencies that have none. RRF discards the scores
and keeps only each search's ordering:
`score = Σ 1 / (60 + rank_in_that_list)`. A chunk both searches found collects
two contributions and rises, with nothing to tune.

**Why keyword hits bypass the threshold.** `MIN_SIMILARITY` gates *semantic*
evidence. An exact keyword match is a different kind of evidence; holding it to
the wrong standard is what made "extension 4417" unanswerable.

**Why `to_or_tsquery` rather than `plainto_tsquery`.** The built-ins AND the
terms. "Who do I contact on extension 4417?" becomes `contact & extens & 4417`,
and the chunk reading "reachable at extension 4417" has no "contact" — so the
AND finds nothing and the one case keyword search exists for is missed. ORing
the lexemes and ranking fixes it.

**Measured effect — honestly, it is small at this corpus size.** On 19 chunks,
across four natural-language questions containing identifiers, hybrid changed
**nothing**: vector search already ranked the right chunk #1 or #2 every time.
The one clear win was a **bare identifier typed alone**:

| Query | Vector-only top 5 | Hybrid top 5 |
|---|---|---|
| `NL-220` | **missed entirely** — 5 chunks passed, none contained it | **rank #2**, correct answer |
| `4417` | rank #1 | rank #1 |
| `NL-114` | rank #1 | rank #1 |

**Cost:** zero extra prompt tokens — `CANDIDATE_COUNT` is 10 per search but the
fused list is trimmed to `MATCH_COUNT` (5). One extra Postgres round trip, run
in parallel with the first.

**Reverse if:** never really — it is cheap and additive. But be clear that on a
small corpus it earns its keep only for bare identifiers. Its value grows with
corpus size, as the chunk holding an identifier gets pushed out of the vector
top-N by semantically closer neighbours.

**Requires:** `schema-hybrid.sql`, run once in the Supabase SQL editor.

## D-016 · Query rewriting before retrieval · **Post-MVP, added 2026-09-20**

**Decision:** When a conversation has history, one cheap model call rewrites the
user's question into a standalone search query before it is embedded. The
**search** uses the rewritten query; the **answer** is generated from the
user's original words.

**Why:** conversation history reaches the generator but never the retriever:

```
history  ------------------------------> buildPrompt -> model
question -> embed -> search -----------> buildPrompt
```

Measured before this change: after a turn about the Operations Director,
*"When did they join?"* retrieved **zero chunks** and returned the refusal,
although the answer is in the document. The question embedded on its own is a
vector pointing nowhere.

**Measured after:**

```
Q: When did they join?
   searched for: "When did the floor supervisor and the Operations Director join?"
   3 chunks -> "The current Operations Director, Marisol Venn, joined Northwind
                Labs in the spring of the third fiscal cycle."
```

**Why the answer still uses the original question.** An answer addressing a
silently reworded question reads wrong. The user asked "when did they join?"
and should not get a reply about "when did Marisol Venn join Northwind Labs?".

**Why the only guard is `history.length === 0`.** A pronoun-spotting heuristic
would skip more calls and would sometimes be wrong; this one is always right,
and the rewriter is instructed to echo the question back unchanged when it is
already standalone. Measured: 2 of 4 turns came back unchanged, so the guard
is doing real work without guessing.

**Cost, measured over a 4-turn conversation:** 3 rewrite calls, 409 input +
30 output tokens, **$0.000079** — about **21%** on top of the answers, or
**$0.00002 per message**. Far less than doubling, because the rewrite prompt
carries only the short transcript while the answer prompt carries ~670 tokens
of retrieved chunks. The real cost is **latency**: one extra round trip before
every follow-up.

**Guarded against a misbehaving rewriter:** an empty result, or one much longer
than the question, is discarded in favour of the original. `temperature: 0`,
because this is a mechanical transformation and identical conversations should
rewrite identically.

**What it does NOT fix.** The Phase 3 wrong-antecedent case survives it. Asked
*"And what is the escort ratio for that group?"*, the rewriter resolved the
reference correctly — *"What is the escort ratio for prospective staff badge
holders?"* — and the model **still** answered about auditors. Retrieval was
fixed; generation was not. Exactly the same split seen with D-015.

**Reverse if:** latency matters more than follow-up questions working, which
would be unusual.

## D-017 · Reworded the grounding instruction · **Post-MVP, added 2026-09-20**

**Decision:** The system prompt in `buildPrompt()` now separates three things
that *"Do not use outside knowledge. Do not guess."* had collapsed into one:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Connecting** facts the context states | **allowed** |
| **Adding** facts the context does not state | **never** |
| **Partial** answers | give the part that is there, say what is missing |

**Why:** Phase 5 caught this instruction failing in *both* directions.

- **Too loose** (5.5, instruction deleted): the bot answered "the capital of
  France is Paris" and wrote a 400-word sourdough recipe while citing
  lab-handbook chunks.
- **Too strict** (as originally written): it refused *"Who do I contact on
  extension 4417?"* with the chunk reading *"...liaison, currently reachable at
  extension 4417"* in front of it, because answering means joining two stated
  facts. "Do not guess" reads, to a model, as "do not reason."

**Measured with a fixed six-case battery** (`scratch/prompt-eval.js`), run
before and after, covering both directions at once:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| direct fact | PASS | PASS |
| **one-step inference** (extension 4417) | **FAIL** | **PASS** |
| wrong-antecedent follow-up | FAIL | FAIL *(see below)* |
| absent fact, same domain (goggles) | PASS | PASS |
| off-topic (France) | PASS | PASS |
| absent fact, plausible (parking spaces) | PASS | PASS |
| | **4/6** | **5/6** |

**The refusals all held.** That was the thing at risk, and it is why the battery
includes three different kinds of absent question rather than one.

### What it did not fix, and what that tells you

**1. The wrong-antecedent case is a model limit, not a prompt limit.** Asked
*"what is the escort ratio for that group?"*, retrieval and query rewriting both
worked perfectly — the rewrite resolved to "prospective staff on site tours" and
the top chunk contained the exact sentence. `gpt-4o-mini` still answered with the
*auditor* exception instead of the general rule.

Swapping one env var to `gpt-4o` and changing nothing else: **6/6**, with
*"The escort ratio for prospective staff on site tours (violet badge holders) is
one staff member per three visitors."*

A second attempt at fixing this in the prompt (an explicit
general-rule-versus-exception instruction) produced **no improvement** and was
removed rather than left in as tokens that buy nothing.

**2. The partial-answer clause does not hold up under a starved retriever.**
Re-running the Phase 5.4 setup (`CHUNK_SIZE` 300, `MATCH_COUNT` 1), where only
the Quiet Hour's *hours* are retrieved and not its *reason*:

- `gpt-4o-mini`: still invents — *"because the building requires a period of
  reduced noise and activity."*
- `gpt-4o`: degrades to circular rather than false — *"because the building has
  a Quiet Hour policy."*

Neither says "the documents do not say why", which is what the instruction asks
for. **An instruction to admit a gap is much weaker than the pull to complete a
sentence.** Worth knowing: this is the failure mode you cannot prompt your way
out of, and the real fix is retrieving enough context in the first place.

**Model kept as `gpt-4o-mini`** (D-005 unchanged). `gpt-4o` scores better on
reasoning over the retrieved text but costs roughly 16× per input token, and
the difference showed up on one contrived case out of six. It is one env var if
that trade ever becomes worth making.

**Reverse if:** the refusals start leaking. `scratch/prompt-eval.js` exists to
catch that — re-run it after any edit to `buildPrompt()`.
